answer: Random re-execution is the whole check: the node reruns one submission in twenty on peers drawn from a rotating pool, and a single upheld challenge revokes the identity's standing back to its anchor. The number that matters is 5%, the share of work an attacker must expect to have rerun by someone with no stake in his lie. Every extra identity adds one more vertex he cannot control in that pool, and his nebula of accounts carries the same 5% exposure per copy.
